title.narrative: Strengthened and Measurable Actions for Resilient and Transformative Health Systems Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The proposed program will support India to consolidate and strengthen its pandemic preparedness and response (PPR) capability through a multipronged and cross-sectoral approach across central and sub-national governments. The related policy actions will lead to improved institutional capacity and mechanisms for infrastructure planning and management in the health sector and will raise India's ability to prevent and mitigate the impact of future public health emergencies and complex systemic risks.

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Mar 01, 2022 - Feb 29, 2024

description.narrative:
Action 1: In order to enhance real-time monitoring of public health emergencies and informed decision making, MOHFW (a) operationalized National Health Emergency Operation Center(N-HeOC) to also monitor implementation during non-emergency times of at least 20 national public health programs, (at least 5 programs will maintain disaggregated data based on sex and age) and (b) issued a framework for establishing and operationalizing state health emergency operation centers (S-HeOCs). Target date: 2024-02-29
Action 2: To strengthen diagnostic capacity, surveillance of emerging and notifiable infectious diseases, and outbreak response at regional, state/UT and metropolitan levels, MOHFW/NCDC provided budget allocations for at least 3 regional BSL-2 branches of National Center for Disease Control (NCDCs), 15 state/Union Territories (UTs) BSL-2 NCDC branches, 10 metropolitan surveillance units, and 5 Bio Safety Level BSL-3 laboratories for FY2022 to FY2026. Target date: 2024-02-29
Action 3: To operationalize One Health approach by ensuring intersectoral preparedness for identification of novel and unknown zoonotic diseases, (a) the Prime Minister's Science, Technology, and Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC) approved the set-up of a National One Health Mission with a cross-ministerial effort which will serve to coordinate, support, and integrate all the existing One Health activities in the country, (b) MOHFW/NCDC operationalized a ‘Center for One Health' with a formalized organogram for effective governance and coordination, and (c) MOHFW/NCDC issued operational guidelines for a national One Health programme for prevention and control of zoonosis. Target date: 2024-02-29

Action 1: Parliament enacted the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission (NNMC) Bill, 2023 to enable comprehensive reforms in the nursing and midwifery sector and to regulate and maintain education and service standards. Target date: 2024-02-29

title.narrative: Policy 2 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Mar 01, 2022 - Feb 29, 2024

description.narrative:
Policy 2: Reform Area 2: Strengthened Human Resources for Health (HRH) Outcome 1: By April 2027, at least five states have introduced new regulations for nursing and midwifery to maintain education and service standards.
Action 2: To ensure that quality is aligned to global standards, the NMC passed regulations for establishing (i) a publicly available National Register which shall contain all the entries of the registered medical practitioners and shall be maintained by the Ethics and Medical Registration Board, (ii) professional conduct, etiquette and ethical practices of registered medical practitioners (iii) new medical institutions, starting of new medical courses or increase of seats for existing courses in addition to assessment and rating of all medical institutions, and (iv) a National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professionals to regulate and maintain education and service standards, oversee professional conduct, and manage online and live Registers. Target date: 2024-02-29
Action 3: To strengthen service delivery by segregating clinical and public health functions, MOHFW issued guidance to states for establishing norms for structured entry and career progression under the Public Health Management Cadre (PHMC). Target date: 2024-02-29
Action 1: To augment public healthcare service delivery to provide for assured treatment and management of patients with infectious diseases or critical illnesses, MOHFW provided budget allocations to at least 5 states for establishment of district integrated public health labs (IPHLs) and critical care hospital blocks (CCBs) for FY2022 to FY2026, and (b) issued technical guidelines to support states for operationalization of IPHLs and CCBs Target date: 2024-02-29

title.narrative: Policy 3 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Mar 01, 2022 - Feb 29, 2024

description.narrative:
Policy 3: Reform Area 3: Expanded Climate Resilient Public Health Infrastructure and Innovative Service Delivery Outcome 1: By 2027, at least five states shall outsource drug distribution from district warehouses to health care facilities via third party logistics provider (public or private).
Action 2: To institutionalize climate and health coordination and prioritization (a) at least 5 states established a Governing Body on Climate Change and Human Health under Hon'ble Health Minister (State) and a Multi-Sectoral Task Force on Climate Change and Human Health under the State Secretary for Health, and (b) MOHFW/NCDC has issued detailed guidelines to support state level establishment of Green and Climate Resilient Healthcare Facilities that are climate-smart, disaster-resilient, and environmentally sustainable. Target date: 2024-02-29
Action 3: To strengthen service delivery through innovations, MOHFW (a) issued operational guidelines for use of drones through public or private operators to ensure last mile delivery in public healthcare facilities, (b) operationalized Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States (Tele MANAS) digital solution and instituted a Network of 23 tele-mental health Centers of Excellence to ensure support for mental health conditions amplified by the pandemic, and (c) launched U-WIN to specifically help track and target left out and dropped out children by digitizing Universal Immunization Program (UIP) covering pregnant women and children (aged 0-5 years) including provision to issue digital vaccination certificates with QR code. Target date: 2024-02-29
